description:
Short title
Raman soft sensor glucose/lactate

What should the AI do?
Our Raman based soft sensor predicts glucose and lactate in the perfusion bioreactors, and the predicted glucose drives the feed pump.

Where will it be used?
Manufacturing / production, MSAT / tech transfer / process development

Does the AI output directly affect a batch, a GMP record, a QC result, a release or a process setting?
Yes, directly. drives the feed pump

What kind of AI is it?
Updates itself in use: new versions go live without a test-and-release step. the vendor's pipeline retrains a candidate model every night on the latest runs

What happens with the output?
Takes effect automatically; nobody checks individual outputs. prediction goes to the feed pump

Who checks the output, and how?
nothing goes live automatically: a new version is only deployed after it passes our re-test and QA approves the change, roughly once a quarter

What data goes into it?
Confidential company data

Who provides it?
Not sure. vendor's pipeline

grid.note: Simplified grid inspired by the GAMP AI adaptiveness × autonomy concept; levels defined in this project.

decision.label: Should not proceed: not for GMP-critical use (Annex 22 §1)
decision.explanation: Draft Annex 22 §1 covers only static, deterministic models in critical GMP applications, and says that dynamic, probabilistic and generative models (including LLMs) should not be used in critical GMP applications. Its human-in-the-loop allowance is given for non-critical use only. This is a reading of the EU draft; FDA's draft credibility guidance instead scales model risk with how much the model influences the decision.

citations.quote: Following the above, the document does not apply to Generative AI and Large Language Models (LLM), and such models should not be used in critical GMP applications.

judgments.label: GMP-critical
judgments.rationale: Keyword baseline: the AI output feeds a GMP decision, record or control ('ticked: Yes, directly').

citations.quote: This annex applies to all types of computerised systems used in the manufacturing of medicinal products and active substances, where Artificial Intelligence models are used in critical applications with direct impact on patient safety, product quality or data integrity, e.g. to predict or classify data.

judgments.label: Dynamic / adaptive model
judgments.rationale: Keyword baseline: the model keeps learning or retraining in operation ('ticked: Updates itself in use: new versions go live without a test-and-release step').

citations.quote: The use of dynamic models which continuously and automatically learn and adapt performance during use, is not covered by this document, and should not be used in critical GMP applications.

judgments.label: AI acts autonomously
judgments.rationale: Keyword baseline: outputs take effect without a human check ('ticked: Takes effect automatically; nobody checks individual outputs').

citations.ref: FDA AI credibility guidance (draft) §IV.A.3 Step 3: Assess the AI model risk
citations.quote: In this example, model influence would likely be estimated to be high because the AI model will be the sole determinant of which type of patient monitoring a participant undergoes.

controls.title: Redesign before any GMP-critical use
controls.what: Under the draft Annex 22 this model type should not be used in a critical GMP application. Options: restrict the use to non-critical support with a human in the loop, or use a static, deterministic model tested under Annex 22.

citations.quote: This annex applies to all types of computerised systems used in the manufacturing of medicinal products and active substances, where Artificial Intelligence models are used in critical applications with direct impact on patient safety, product quality or data integrity, e.g. to predict or classify data.

controls.title: Documented quality risk assessment
controls.what: A justified, documented risk assessment sets the extent of validation and data-integrity controls; formality proportional to risk.
controls.why: Source: Annex 11 (2011) §1 Risk Management; ICH Q9(R1) §4.3 Risk Assessment; ICH Q9(R1) §5.1 Formality in Quality Risk Management

citations.quote: As part of a risk management system, decisions on the extent of validation and data integrity controls should be based on a justified and documented risk assessment of the computerised system.
Risk assessment consists of the identification of hazards and the analysis and evaluation of risks associated with exposure to those hazards (as defined below).

citations.ref: ICH Q9(R1) §5.1 Formality in Quality Risk Management
citations.quote: The following may be characteristics of higher levels of formality: • All parts of the quality risk management process (risk assessment, risk control, risk review and risk communication) are explicitly performed, and stand-alone quality risk management reports or related documents which address all aspects of the…

controls.title: EU AI Act screening
controls.what: Check whether the system is high-risk (Art. 6, Annex III; e.g. AI used in recruitment or worker management) and, if so, meet the deployer duties of Art. 26. Ensure AI literacy of staff (Art. 4). Transparency duties (Art. 50) fall mainly on the provider; as deployer, check they are met.
controls.why: Source: EU AI Act: Article 6: Classification rules for high-risk AI systems; EU AI Act: Annex III: High-risk AI systems referred to in Article 6(2); EU AI Act: Article 26: Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems; EU AI Act: Article 4: AI literacy; EU AI Act: Article 50: Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems

citations.ref: EU AI Act: Article 6: Classification rules for high-risk AI systems
citations.quote: A provider who considers that an AI system referred to in Annex III is not high-risk shall document its assessment before that system is placed on the market or put into service.

citations.ref: EU AI Act: Annex III: High-risk AI systems referred to in Article 6(2)
citations.quote: Employment, workers’ management and access to self-employment: (a) AI systems intended to be used for the recruitment or selection of natural persons, in particular to place targeted job advertisements, to analyse and filter job applications, and to evaluate candidates;

citations.ref: EU AI Act: Article 26: Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems
citations.quote: Without prejudice to paragraphs 1 and 2, to the extent the deployer exercises control over the input data, that deployer shall ensure that input data is relevant and sufficiently representative in view of the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system.

citations.ref: EU AI Act: Article 4: AI literacy
citations.quote: Providers and deployers of AI systems shall take measures to ensure, to their best extent, a sufficient level of AI literacy of their staff and other persons dealing with the operation and use of AI systems on their behalf, taking into account their technical knowledge, experience, education and training and the…

citations.ref: EU AI Act: Article 50: Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems
citations.quote: Providers of AI systems, including general-purpose AI systems, generating synthetic audio, image, video or text content, shall ensure that the outputs of the AI system are marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated.

warnings: Draft Annex 22, the draft Annex 11 and the draft Chapter 4 are consultation drafts (July 2025). The final texts may differ.
